newsitem.title: MALI: Mali court cancels election results.
newsitem.headline: Mali court cancels election results.

text.p: Mali's constitutional court has scrapped results of the West African nation's chaotic April 13 parliamentary elections, citing irregularities.
The second round of parliamentary elections, due on Sunday, will not take place and a question mark now hangs over the presidential election, originally set for May 4.

An official of the Independent National Electoral Commission told Reuters that none of the 10 presidential candidates, including President Alpha Omar Konare, had confirmed their candidacy by a noon Saturday deadline.
"The different opposition candidates stood down following the confusion that reigned during the first round of the parliamentary election on April 13," he said.
The ruling of the court, announced in a special session late on Friday and covering results nationwide, means that Sunday's planned second round will not now take place.

But it was not immediately clear what would happen next, with the opposition demanding the suspension of all phases of this year's elections, only the second multi-party national vote since independence from France in 1960.
"The court has noted that numerous irregularities seriously tainted the sincerity and transparency of the vote on April 13," court president Abdoulaye Dicko said, personally reading the ruling.
The opposition had been demanding the scrapping of the poll. Problems with organisation and a lack of ballot papers prevented many of the voters who turned out in force from casting their vote.
President Alpha Oumar Konare, a historian elected during Mali's widely praised 1992 democratic transition, had said he would abide by the decision of the court.

The April 13 election for a new 147-seat parliament, to be followed by presidential and municipal elections on May 4 and June 1, are a test of how deeply democracy has taken root in the poor West African nation.
The opposition has been calling for the whole process to be suspended and reorganised and has threatened to disrupt polling if it goes ahead.
Konare, who has steered Mali on a course of economic liberalisation, has said the electoral timetable should be respected. The court did not rule on that issue.
